table_name: GPU Trace Frontend Necessity Workload Evidence Catalog
description: Workload catalog covering AI training scale tiers, with microbenchmark cases listed as controls. GPT-2 small excluded from evidence line per plan decision.

workloads.approximate_scale: 110M parameters, single encoder layer, ~7M parameters per layer
workloads.notes: Primary claim-bearing workload at slice granularity. Single transformer encoder layer captures representative compute and memory patterns.

workloads.approximate_scale: 110M parameters, full forward+backward pass, batch scaling from small upward

batch_scaling.strategy: scale upward until resource ceiling reached

workloads.notes: Primary claim-bearing workload at step granularity. Batch scaling records are separate (see task13).

workloads.approximate_scale: 8B parameters, single decoder layer, ~200M parameters per layer (grouped-query attention, SwiGLU FFN)
workloads.notes: Represents modern decoder-only architecture at industrial scale. Larger than BERT encoder layer due to GQA and wider FFN.

Non-blocking tail attempt. Only attempted after required evidence line (BERT-base full step, Llama 3.1 8B slice) is complete. Repeated failures do not invalidate required artifacts. Records attempt count, failure reason, and partial artifacts.

controls.notes: Existing measured microbenchmarks serve as controls for trace-size, export-time, and sim-time baselines. Not used as primary AI-training evidence.
HPC benchmarks provide diversity in trace patterns but are not AI-training workloads. Listed as appendix material.
MLPerf full workloads are scale anchors at infeasible simulation cost. Used only to contextualize the gap between measured workloads and production scale. Not part of the claim-bearing evidence.

excluded.reason: Too small for intended evidence line. Would not provide meaningful P_trace_to_sim signal for AI-training scale.
Multi-GPU communication class. Different problem domain from single-GPU trace frontend study.
MPI/network benchmark class. Irrelevant to GPU trace-driven frontend study.
